edits.find:
A 20-year-old is below the screening floor. Sexual debut at 15, five partners, inconsistent condoms — every one of those raises HPV exposure and none of them lowers the starting age. The answer is no cytology; screening begins at 21.

The rule is deliberately risk-blind. HPV in adolescents is near-universal and clears in ~90% within 2 years; progression to cancer takes a decade-plus. Screening early finds transient infection and produces excisional procedures (LEEP) that raise preterm-birth risk in women who were never going to develop cancer. That's why cervical cancer under 21 is rare — and why screening her would harm without benefit.
edits.with:
A 20-year-old is below the screening floor. Sexual debut at 15, five partners and inconsistent condom use each raise HPV (human papillomavirus) exposure, but none of them lowers the starting age. She needs no cytology; screening begins at 21.

The age floor deliberately ignores individual risk. HPV infection in adolescents is near-universal and clears in ~90% within 2 years. Progression to cancer takes more than a decade. Early screening finds transient infection and leads to excisional procedures (LEEP) that raise preterm-birth risk in women who were never going to develop cancer. Cervical cancer under 21 is therefore rare. Screening her would cause harm without benefit.

edits.find: Correction to an earlier framing in this document The Part I pregnancy-vaccine brief listed Tdap's trap as "Timing — 27–36 weeks," which reads like an eligibility gate. It isn't. Tdap is safe at any gestational age, and if a pregnant woman has a wound requiring tetanus prophylaxis, or is caught in a pertussis outbreak, you give it then. 27–36 weeks is an optimization of transplacental IgG transfer, not a permission window. Gate vs. optimization is exactly the distinction NBME builds a question on.

edits.find:
The stem has already met the diagnostic threshold. PID is a presumptive clinical diagnosis, and the gate is deliberately low: a sexually active young woman with pelvic pain, no other identified cause, and any one of cervical motion tenderness, uterine tenderness, or adnexal tenderness. She has cervical motion tenderness, and the purulent discharge plus fever above 38.3 C are supporting criteria.

The threshold sits there because treatment prevents the sequelae and delay causes them. Managing the alternatives — ectopic pregnancy, appendicitis, ovarian cyst, torsion — is not impaired by starting antimicrobials. There is no diagnostic penalty for treating early and a permanent one for treating late: infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain.
edits.with:
PID (pelvic inflammatory disease) is a presumptive clinical diagnosis with a deliberately low threshold. The minimum criteria are a sexually active young woman with pelvic pain, no other identified cause, and any one of cervical motion tenderness, uterine tenderness or adnexal tenderness. She meets the threshold with cervical motion tenderness. Her purulent discharge and fever above 38.3 C are supporting criteria.

The threshold is low because treatment prevents the sequelae and delay causes them. Management of the alternatives (ectopic pregnancy, appendicitis, ovarian cyst, torsion) is not impaired by starting antimicrobials. Treating early carries no diagnostic penalty. Treating late carries a permanent penalty: infertility, ectopic pregnancy and chronic pelvic pain.
